title: two tiny tables, every ON and every join kind, from postgres itself

steps.sql: SELECT name, city FROM customers ORDER BY CASE name WHEN 'Ada' THEN 1 WHEN 'Alan' THEN 2 WHEN 'Grace' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END
steps.note: the left table, in the order the grid draws it.

steps.sql: SELECT city, store FROM stores ORDER BY CASE store WHEN 'soho' THEN 1 WHEN 'marais' THEN 2 WHEN 'mitte' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END
steps.note: the right table, in the order the grid draws it.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c JOIN stores AS s ON s.city = c.city ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: the equi-join: a pair survives when the cities are equal. Edsger's NULL equals nothing, not even the online store's NULL.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c JOIN stores AS s ON true ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: ON true keeps every pair: 4 × 4 = 16 rows. that's CROSS JOIN.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c JOIN stores AS s ON s.city <> c.city ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: the cities differ: 6 pairs. a NULL city is unknown against everything, so Edsger and the online store sit this one out too.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c JOIN stores AS s ON s.city = c.city AND s.store <> 'soho' ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: equal cities, and not the soho store: ON can test anything, from either side.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c JOIN stores AS s ON s.city IS NOT DISTINCT FROM c.city ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: IS NOT DISTINCT FROM treats two NULLs as the same, so Edsger finally meets the online store.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c JOIN stores AS s ON false ORDER BY c.name, s.store
SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN stores AS s ON s.city = c.city ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: LEFT JOIN, equal cities: the 3 pairs, plus Edsger, who matched nobody, padded with NULLs.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN stores AS s ON true ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: LEFT JOIN, ON true: every customer already has a partner, so there's nobody to pad.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN stores AS s ON s.city <> c.city ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: LEFT JOIN, the cities differ: the 6 pairs, plus Edsger again.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN stores AS s ON s.city = c.city AND s.store <> 'soho' ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: LEFT JOIN, equal and not soho: only Grace keeps a partner. Ada and Alan lost theirs to the ON, so they come back padded.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN stores AS s ON s.city IS NOT DISTINCT FROM c.city ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: LEFT JOIN, IS NOT DISTINCT FROM: every customer has a partner now, Edsger included.

steps.sql: SELECT c.name, c.city, s.city, s.store FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN stores AS s ON false ORDER BY c.name, s.store
steps.note: LEFT JOIN, ON false: no pair survives, so every customer comes back once, padded. a LEFT JOIN never has fewer rows than its left table.
